result.title: Coordinated Use of Large Language Models in Academic Research
result.comment: 22 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. English translation of an article originally published in Bulgarian in Media and Language (2026). The original Bulgarian publication remains the version of record
result.summary: This study proposes a methodological framework for the coordinated use of multiple large language models in academic research. Its central argument is that involving more models does not in itself guarantee more reliable results; what matters is how cognitive and verification operations are organised. The framework is based on seven principles (procedural independence, functional allocation, the diagnostic value of divergence, the diagnostic value of convergence, external verification, proportionality of checking, and human epistemic responsibility) and sets out a non-linear multi-LLM protocol in which independently obtained results are compared, critically examined and, where necessary, verified against external sources. The approach is illustrated through real-world cases drawn from research practice. The study concludes that moving from a single language model to a coordinated multi-LLM process represents a change in the organisation of research, in which the researcher makes the final decisions and bears scholarly responsibility.

AI.brief_summary: 提出多 LLM 协同开展学术研究的方法论框架，以程序独立、功能分配、分歧与收敛的诊断价值、外部验证、核查比例性等七项原则组织一个非线性协议，并用实际研究案例加以说明。
AI.relevance_reason: 「分歧/收敛的诊断价值」与「核查比例性」可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、何时停止追加检查及多路径贡献分配的后果表述，但领域较远，仅属概念层面的启发线索。
